env.name: cmv
env.description:
2,000 Reddit r/ChangeMyView discussions (balanced). One row = one post with its counter-argument comments.
Columns:
  - post_created_utc: Unix timestamp of the original post (no comment times).
  - title: the original poster's (OP) post heading / claim statement.
  - argument: the OP's explanation of their view (the post body). May contain quotes and marked edits.
  - OC_comments: JSON-encoded list of counter-argument comments written by OTHER users (not the OP).
    List order is not rank or chronology. Row-level measures must say whether they mean any comment,
    all comments, an average, or a count.
  - conversation: formatted discussion text overlapping OC_comments; may include later replies and
    explicit view-change announcements (outcome leakage) — avoid unless interaction is required.
  - log_length: supplied log-transformed length measure (undocumented construction).
  - post_score: the original post's observed Reddit score at collection.
  - delta: OUTCOME, 1 if the OP changed their view, else 0. Never a predictor.
  - post_id, comment_id: identifiers, never predictors.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where the original argument includes explicit comparisons to established scientific or historical norms are associated with lower view change than those without such comparisons.

features.name: argument_compares_to_established_norms
features.definition: OP argument (post body, current text incl. marked edits): 1 if it explicitly compares the OP's claim, position or subject to established scientific or historical norms, else 0
features.spec: Read the argument column only (current text, including marked edits; the OP's own text, excluding quoted external text unless the OP adopts it). Return 1 if the OP explicitly draws a comparison between their claim, position or the subject under discussion and an established scientific norm (e.g. accepted scientific findings, standards, consensus) or an established historical norm (e.g. historical precedent, longstanding historical standards or practice). The comparison must be explicit, not merely a passing mention of science or history. Return 0 if the argument is assessable and has no such comparison. Return null if argument is missing or malformed.

decomposed.h0: Mean delta does not differ between discussions with and without argument_compares_to_established_norms.
decomposed.h1: Discussions with argument_compares_to_established_norms=1 have lower delta than those with 0.
decomposed.note: "Established norms" is interpreted as accepted scientific or historical standards/precedents; boundary is somewhat subjective. Uses current argument text, no initial snapshot.

decomposed.hypothesis: Arguments expressing explicit fear of social rejection or isolation are associated with lower view-change rates than arguments stating beliefs without emotional self-defense.

features.name: op_expresses_fear_of_social_rejection_or_isolation
features.definition: OP's own title and post body: 1 if the OP explicitly expresses fear of social rejection or isolation (e.g., being ostracized, disliked, excluded, left alone) tied to their view or holding/sharing it.
features.spec: Read title and argument (current text, including marked edits) jointly. Return 1 if the OP, in their own voice, explicitly states fear or worry of social rejection or isolation (being rejected, ostracized, excluded, judged by others, losing friends/community, ending up alone) as a feeling or concern. Implicit tone without an explicit statement of such fear gives 0. Exclude text quoted from others, reported opponents' positions, and moderator/bot notices unless the OP explicitly adopts them. Return 0 if the text is assessable and has no such statement. Return null if both title and argument are missing or malformed. Output 1/0/null.

features.name: op_states_belief_without_emotional_self_defense
features.definition: OP's own title and post body: 1 if the OP states beliefs/claims with no emotional self-defense (no expressed fear, hurt, defensiveness or emotional self-protection against others' reactions).
features.spec: Read title and argument (current text, including marked edits) jointly. Return 1 if the OP, in their own voice, states their belief and reasons and contains no emotional self-defense, i.e. no expressed fear of rejection/isolation, and no defensive emotional self-protection (pre-emptive pleas for gentleness, expressions of feeling attacked, hurt or anxious about others' reactions). Return 0 if any such emotional self-defense or fear of social rejection/isolation is present. Exclude quoted external text, reported opponents' positions and moderator/bot notices unless adopted by the OP. Return null if both title and argument are missing or malformed. Output 1/0/null.

decomposed.h0: Mean delta rate does not differ between posts with op_expresses_fear_of_social_rejection_or_isolation and posts with op_states_belief_without_emotional_self_defense (beta_fear = beta_plain).
decomposed.h1: Posts with op_expresses_fear_of_social_rejection_or_isolation have a lower view-change rate than posts with op_states_belief_without_emotional_self_defense (beta_fear < beta_plain).
decomposed.note: The claim is a contrast between two named groups (fear vs plain-belief). In this OLS each coefficient is relative to the residual group (posts with other emotional self-defense but no explicit fear), so neither coefficient alone is the fear-minus-plain difference (beta_fear - beta_plain); that would need a linear-contrast test or subsetting to the two groups, not a single design-matrix term. The two features are mutually exclusive by construction. 'Emotional self-defense' is operationalized per the spec and is not a validated instrument. Hypothesis speaks of 'arguments'; read as the OP's title and post body.

decomposed.hypothesis: Counter-arguments that cite specific, functioning institutional precedents are associated with a higher probability of view change than those relying on abstract normative principles.

features.name: any_comment_cites_functioning_institutional_precedent
features.definition: Counter-argument comments (OC_comments): any comment cites a specific, functioning institutional precedent (a concrete existing institution, policy, law or system that operates/has operated in practice) in support of its argument.
features.spec: Read OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than the OP). Return 1 if at least one comment cites a specific institutional precedent (e.g., a particular existing law, policy, court, organization or system in a named or clearly identifiable jurisdiction/institution) presented as actually functioning or having functioned in practice, used to support the comment's argument. Examples are nonexhaustive; no external verification needed. Return 0 if no comment does so (generic or hypothetical institutions, purely abstract principles, or non-functioning/proposed-only institutions do not count). Empty list gives 0; missing or malformed OC_comments gives null. Do not use other columns.

features.name: any_comment_relies_on_abstract_normative_principles
features.definition: Counter-argument comments (OC_comments): any comment relies on abstract normative principles (general moral/ethical/political principles or values) as its argument basis.
features.spec: Read OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than the OP). Return 1 if at least one comment argues mainly by appeal to abstract normative principles (general moral, ethical, rights, justice, fairness or value principles stated in general terms) rather than a specific concrete example. Return 0 if no comment does. A comment may also cite precedents; count it only if abstract normative principles are a substantial basis of its argument. Empty list gives 0; missing or malformed gives null. Do not use other columns.

decomposed.h0: Coefficient of any_comment_cites_functioning_institutional_precedent is zero (given any_comment_relies_on_abstract_normative_principles) for view-change probability.
decomposed.h1: Coefficient of any_comment_cites_functioning_institutional_precedent is positive relative to any_comment_relies_on_abstract_normative_principles in the model.
decomposed.note: The claim is a contrast between precedent-citing and abstract-principle comments; the single coefficient tests precedent holding principle fixed, not the difference of the two coefficients. Features are row-level any-comment indicators, not comment-level comparisons; the two can overlap within a row. Linear probability model.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions featuring longer precomputed log-transformed discussion length are associated with a higher likelihood of the original poster changing their view.

features.name: log_length_value
features.definition: Row: supplied precomputed log-transformed discussion length value (log_length), unchanged
features.spec: Return pd.to_numeric(df['log_length'], errors='coerce') per row; null if missing or non-numeric. Observed range about 0.69 to 7.44, no missing values. Construction of the measure is undocumented; use as supplied, no recomputation.

decomposed.h0: log_length_value has no association with the probability that the OP changed their view (coefficient = 0).
decomposed.h1: Higher log_length_value is associated with a higher likelihood of OP view change (coefficient > 0).
decomposed.note: log_length's construction is undocumented (unclear what text it measures); used as supplied. OLS on a binary outcome is a linear probability model.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where the original argument contains explicit admissions of uncertainty are associated with a higher probability of view change than those asserting absolute certainty.

features.name: op_explicit_uncertainty_admission
features.definition: OP's own argument text (post body): 1 if the OP explicitly admits uncertainty or possible error in their own view
features.spec: Read only the argument column (current text, including marked edits). Return 1 if the OP, in their own voice, explicitly expresses uncertainty about their view or admits they could be wrong or lack knowledge (e.g. 'I'm not sure', 'I may be wrong', 'I could be mistaken'). Exclude quoted external text, opponents' positions reported by the OP, and moderator/bot notices unless the OP adopts them. Generic hedging words without an explicit admission do not count. Return 0 if the argument is present and has no such admission. Return null if argument is missing or malformed.

features.name: op_asserts_absolute_certainty
features.definition: OP's own argument text (post body): 1 if the OP explicitly asserts absolute certainty or that their view cannot be wrong
features.spec: Read only the argument column (current text, including marked edits). Return 1 if the OP, in their own voice, explicitly asserts absolute certainty about their view (e.g. 'I am 100% certain', 'there is no possible way I'm wrong', 'undeniably true'). Merely confident or opinionated tone does not count. Exclude quoted external text and reported opponents' positions. Return 0 if argument is present and has no such assertion. Return null if argument is missing or malformed.

decomposed.h0: Discussions whose op_explicit_uncertainty_admission is 1 have the same probability of view change as those where it is 0.
decomposed.h1: Discussions with op_explicit_uncertainty_admission = 1 have a higher probability of view change than those with it = 0.
decomposed.note: The claim contrasts uncertainty admissions with absolute-certainty assertions. Absolute certainty is not the complement of uncertainty, and the two features can both be 0. The regression compares uncertainty present with absent. It therefore does not isolate the contrast with posts asserting absolute certainty, which are probably rare. op_asserts_absolute_certainty is defined for that comparison but is not in the rhs. Frequency and intensity thresholds are unspecified. It tests association only, not causation.

decomposed.hypothesis: Counter-arguments frequently challenging multiple distinct factual premises within the argument are positively associated with view change.

features.name: distinct_factual_premises_challenged_count
features.definition: Counter-argument comments (OC_comments): number of distinct factual premises in the OP's title/argument that are challenged by at least one comment
features.spec: Read title, argument (OP post body, current text incl. marked edits) and OC_comments (JSON list of comments by other users; order carries no meaning) jointly. Count the distinct factual (empirical/descriptive, not purely evaluative, moral or logical-structure) premises stated or clearly relied on in the OP's title/argument that at least one comment explicitly challenges, disputes, or presents evidence against. Deduplicate semantically: the same premise challenged by several comments counts once; different premises count separately. Do not count challenges to values, definitions-as-preference, or merely adding new considerations; do not count premises only mentioned by comments and not in the OP text. Output a non-negative integer: 0 = no comment challenges any OP factual premise. If OC_comments is a valid empty list return 0. If title/argument or OC_comments is missing or malformed return null. Do not use the conversation or any outcome.

decomposed.h0: distinct_factual_premises_challenged_count has no association with view change (coefficient = 0).
decomposed.h1: Higher distinct_factual_premises_challenged_count is associated with a higher probability of view change (coefficient > 0).
decomposed.note: The hypothesis says "frequently" challenging "multiple" premises without a frequency cutoff; none was invented. The count of distinct factual premises challenged across all comments is used as an operational graded measure, not a thresholded "frequent" indicator. Comments are an unordered list, so per-comment frequency/chronology is not captured. Linear model on binary outcome (OLS).

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where the original argument contains fewer counter-argument responses are associated with a lower likelihood of the original poster changing their view.

features.name: oc_comment_count
features.definition: OC_comments list: number of counter-argument comments (list length).
features.spec: Parse OC_comments as a JSON list of strings. Output len(list) as a non-negative integer. A valid empty list gives 0. Missing or unparseable JSON gives null. Do not deduplicate or read other columns.

decomposed.h0: oc_comment_count has no association with the likelihood of the OP changing their view (coefficient = 0).
decomposed.h1: Higher oc_comment_count is associated with a higher likelihood of the OP changing their view (coefficient > 0), i.e., fewer comments mean lower likelihood.
decomposed.note: The hypothesis wording ("original argument contains fewer counter-argument responses") is ambiguous. It is interpreted as the number of counter-argument comments supplied in OC_comments for the row. The supplied list may not be the complete discussion, and its order is not chronological. The test is a linear (OLS) association on the delta outcome and does not control for confounds.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions with at least three distinct counter-arguments in the posted comments are associated with a higher likelihood of the original poster changing their view.

features.name: distinct_counter_argument_count
features.definition: Counter-argument comments by other users in OC_comments: number of distinct counter-arguments to the OP's view (semantically deduplicated)
features.spec: Read the OC_comments JSON list (comments by users other than the OP; order carries no rank or chronology). Count the distinct counter-arguments to the OP's view made across these comments, merging comments or passages that make essentially the same argument into one. Only count argumentative points opposing the OP's position; do not count pleasantries, clarifying questions, or agreement alone. One comment may contain several distinct counter-arguments. Output a non-negative integer. A valid empty list gives 0; missing or malformed OC_comments gives null. Do not use the conversation column or later replies.

features.name: has_at_least_three_distinct_counter_arguments
features.definition: Counter-argument comments: 1 if distinct_counter_argument_count >= 3, else 0
features.spec: Using feature distinct_counter_argument_count: return null if it is null; else 1 if value >= 3 else 0. E.g. (df.distinct_counter_argument_count>=3).astype(float), with null preserved.

decomposed.h0: Discussions with has_at_least_three_distinct_counter_arguments = 1 have the same likelihood of OP view change as those with 0.
decomposed.h1: Discussions with has_at_least_three_distinct_counter_arguments = 1 have a higher likelihood of OP view change than those with 0.
decomposed.note: Distinct counter-arguments are semantically deduplicated and counted within the supplied OC_comments only; the list may be incomplete relative to the full discussion. OLS on binary outcome is a linear probability model.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where the original post title uses absolute certainty markers are associated with a lower likelihood of the original poster changing their view.

features.name: title_absolute_certainty_marker
features.definition: OP post title: contains at least one absolute certainty marker (e.g., universal or categorical wording expressing total certainty)
features.spec: Read only the title. Return 1 if the title itself uses at least one absolute certainty marker, i.e. wording that presents the claim as completely certain or exceptionless (e.g. 'all', 'always', 'never', 'every', 'no one', 'definitely', 'undeniably', 'obviously', 'absolutely', 'impossible'). The examples are nonexhaustive. Return 0 if the title has no such marker (including hedged or ordinary claims). Ignore the 'CMV:' prefix itself. Return null if the title is missing or empty.

decomposed.h0: Title_absolute_certainty_marker has no association with the likelihood of the OP changing their view.
decomposed.h1: Title_absolute_certainty_marker = 1 is associated with a lower likelihood of the OP changing their view.
decomposed.note: Binary presence of a marker; "absolute certainty markers" has no fixed lexicon, so the examples are nonexhaustive. Linear probability model on binary delta. Uses the current title text.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where original posts explicitly invite critique or use tentative language are associated with higher view-change rates than those using absolute, definitive declarations.

features.name: op_invites_critique_or_tentative
features.definition: OP's own title and post body (current text, including marked edits; excluding quoted others' text): 1 if it explicitly invites critique/challenge or uses tentative language (explicit uncertainty or possible error), else 0.
features.spec: Read title and argument together. Return 1 if the OP, in their own voice, explicitly invites critique, counterarguments or challenge to their view (e.g. asking to be shown wrong) OR expresses explicit tentativeness, uncertainty, or admits they may be mistaken regarding their view. Ignore quoted external text, reported opponents' positions and moderator/bot notices unless the OP adopts them. Use supplied current text including marked edits; do not infer an original snapshot. Return 0 if neither is present. Return null if both title and argument are missing or malformed. Generic CMV boilerplate counts only if it explicitly invites critique. Absolute certainty is not treated as the complement.

features.name: op_absolute_definitive_declaration
features.definition: OP's own title and post body (current text, including marked edits; excluding quoted others' text): 1 if it states its view using absolute, definitive declarations, else 0.
features.spec: Read title and argument together. Return 1 if the OP, in their own voice, states their view as absolute, certain or definitive (e.g. categorical claims with no hedging, declaring the view unquestionably true). Ignore quoted external text, reported opponents' positions and moderator/bot notices unless adopted by the OP. Use supplied current text including marked edits; do not infer an original snapshot. Return 0 if no such absolute declaration is present (including purely tentative or neutral posts). Return null if both title and argument are missing or malformed. This is assessed independently of the invites/tentative feature; a post may be 1 on both or neither.

decomposed.h0: View-change rates do not differ between posts with op_invites_critique_or_tentative=1 and posts with op_absolute_definitive_declaration=1.
decomposed.h1: Posts with op_invites_critique_or_tentative=1 have higher view-change rates than posts with op_absolute_definitive_declaration=1.
decomposed.note: Claim is a contrast between two named groups (tentative/inviting vs absolute). In the OLS with both indicators, beta_A - beta_B is not a single design-matrix coefficient, so no single term represents it; term=null. The two features are not complements and may overlap or both be 0. Uses current post text including edits; no initial snapshot available.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions featuring counter-arguments that explicitly cite specific real-world examples are associated with higher likelihood of original view change.

features.name: any_comment_cites_specific_real_world_example
features.definition: Counter-argument comments (OC_comments): 1 if any comment explicitly cites a specific real-world example in support of its argument, else 0
features.spec: Read OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than the OP; order carries no meaning). Output 1 if at least one comment explicitly cites a specific real-world example (a particular identifiable real event, person, case, organization, place, study, product or concrete documented instance, not a purely hypothetical, generic or vague 'some people' reference) as support for its argument. Named examples in the construct are nonexhaustive; no external verification is required. Quotes of others do not count unless the commenter uses them as a specific example. Output 0 if the list is valid and no comment does so. Empty list gives 0; missing or malformed input gives null.

decomposed.h0: any_comment_cites_specific_real_world_example has no association with the likelihood of OP view change.
decomposed.h1: any_comment_cites_specific_real_world_example is positively associated with the likelihood of OP view change.
decomposed.note: Hypothesis is associative; OLS on binary delta is a linear probability model. Uses current comment text; list order is not chronology. No controls added.

decomposed.hypothesis: Counterarguments containing measured, logical reasoning are positively associated with the original poster changing their mind compared to those containing emotional aggression in ChangeMyView discussions.

features.name: any_comment_measured_logical_reasoning
features.definition: Counter-argument comments (OC_comments): 1 if any comment contains measured, logical reasoning, else 0
features.spec: Read the OC_comments JSON list (comments by users other than the OP; list order carries no rank or chronology). Return 1 if at least one comment contains measured, logical reasoning: a calm, even-toned argument that proceeds through explicit reasons, evidence, or inferences toward its point (it may disagree with the OP). Generic politeness without reasoning does not count; reasoning delivered in an emotionally aggressive tone is not 'measured'. Quoted text from others is not the commenter's own reasoning unless adopted. Return 0 if the list is valid and no comment qualifies, or if the list is empty. Return null if OC_comments is missing or malformed. Use only current supplied text.

features.name: any_comment_emotional_aggression
features.definition: Counter-argument comments (OC_comments): 1 if any comment expresses emotional aggression, else 0
features.spec: Read the OC_comments JSON list (comments by users other than the OP; order carries no rank or chronology). Return 1 if at least one comment's own text shows emotional aggression: hostile, angry, insulting, contemptuous, or belittling language or tone directed at the OP or others (e.g. personal attacks, sneering, hostile profanity). Mere disagreement, blunt or critical but civil statements, and generic emotional words without hostility do not count. Quoted text from others is excluded unless adopted by the commenter. Return 0 if the list is valid and no comment qualifies, or if the list is empty. Return null if OC_comments is missing or malformed. Use only current supplied text.

features.name: logical_minus_aggressive_any
features.definition: Row-level contrast: any_comment_measured_logical_reasoning minus any_comment_emotional_aggression (range -1 to 1)
features.spec: df['any_comment_measured_logical_reasoning'] - df['any_comment_emotional_aggression']; null if either is null. 1 = logical reasoning present without aggression; 0 = both or neither present; -1 = aggression present without measured logical reasoning.

decomposed.h0: logical_minus_aggressive_any has zero association with the OP changing their view.
decomposed.h1: logical_minus_aggressive_any is positively associated with the OP changing their view.
decomposed.note: Hypothesis compares comments with measured logical reasoning vs emotional aggression; operationalized at row level as any-comment indicators and their difference (a row-level proxy, not a comment-level comparison). Rows with both or neither score 0, so the contrast mixes distinct situations and assumes equal and opposite effects. Any vs share/frequency is not specified in the claim. Comment order is unknown; conversation not used (leakage).

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where counter-arguments explicitly quote and refute specific factual claims in the original post are associated with higher rates of view change.

features.name: any_comment_quotes_and_refutes_op_factual_claim
features.definition: Counter-argument comments (OC_comments): any comment explicitly quotes (or directly reproduces) a specific factual claim from the OP's title/argument and refutes it
features.spec: Read title, argument (OP post body, including marked edits) and OC_comments (JSON list of comments by other users; order is not chronology) jointly. Return 1 if at least one comment explicitly quotes or closely reproduces a specific factual claim made in the OP's title or argument (a verbatim or near-verbatim excerpt, e.g. markdown quote block or quotation marks, that matches OP text) AND then disputes/refutes that factual claim (argues it is false, inaccurate or unsupported). Quote must be of a factual claim, not merely opinion/value; refutation need not be correct. Quoting without refuting, refuting without explicit quote, or only topic mention gives 0. Return 0 if OC_comments is a valid empty list. Return null if title/argument or OC_comments is missing or malformed so that the judgment cannot be made. Do not use the conversation column or any later replies.

decomposed.h0: any_comment_quotes_and_refutes_op_factual_claim has no association with delta (view change rate).
decomposed.h1: any_comment_quotes_and_refutes_op_factual_claim is associated with a higher rate of view change (delta).
decomposed.note: The hypothesis does not specify any vs. all vs. frequency; 'any comment' is used as the operationalization. OLS on binary delta is a linear probability model. Association only, not causal. Factual vs opinion boundary is a semantic judgment.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where counter-arguments explicitly validate the original poster's personal dignity or effort before introducing corrective logic are associated with higher view-change rates than purely logical refutations.

features.name: any_comment_validates_op_dignity_or_effort_before_correction
features.definition: Counter-argument comments (OC_comments): any comment explicitly validates the OP's personal dignity or effort and only afterward introduces corrective logic
features.spec: Read OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than the OP), with title and argument as context for what the OP said. Return 1 if at least one comment first explicitly affirms the OP's personal worth/dignity or effort (e.g. praising their thoughtfulness, effort, sincerity, or respecting them as a person; not merely agreeing with a point or generic politeness) and then, later in the same comment, introduces corrective or disagreeing reasoning. Validation must be directed at the OP, not at third parties or quoted text. Validation appearing only after the correction, or with no corrective logic, does not count. Return 0 if the list is valid and no comment meets this. Return null if OC_comments is missing or malformed. Ignore the conversation column and any later replies. Empty list gives 0.

features.name: all_comments_purely_logical_refutation
features.definition: Counter-argument comments (OC_comments): all comments are purely logical refutations with no explicit validation of the OP's personal dignity or effort
features.spec: Read OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than the OP). Return 1 if every comment consists of corrective/refuting reasoning or evidence and none contains explicit validation of the OP's personal worth, dignity or effort (generic politeness or agreement with a point is not validation). Return 0 if the list is nonempty and at least one comment explicitly validates the OP's dignity or effort or does not primarily present refuting reasoning. Return null if OC_comments is missing, malformed, or an empty list. Do not use the conversation column.

decomposed.h0: Discussions with any_comment_validates_op_dignity_or_effort_before_correction and discussions with all_comments_purely_logical_refutation have equal view-change rates.
decomposed.h1: Discussions with any_comment_validates_op_dignity_or_effort_before_correction have higher view-change rates than discussions with all_comments_purely_logical_refutation.
decomposed.note: The claim contrasts validate-then-correct with purely logical discussions, i.e. beta_validate - beta_pure, which is not a single coefficient here (each is relative to an omitted residual group). Ordering of validation before correction is judged within a comment only; comment list order is not chronology. The pure feature is null for empty lists.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions featuring counter-arguments that provide concrete real-world examples are associated with a higher likelihood of view change than those relying primarily on abstract reasoning.

features.name: any_comment_concrete_real_world_example
features.definition: Counter-argument comments (OC_comments): any comment provides a concrete real-world example (specific real-world case, instance, event, person, or documented situation) in support of its argument
features.spec: Read the OC_comments JSON list (comments by users other than OP). Return 1 if at least one comment provides a concrete real-world example, i.e. a specific actual case, instance, event, person, organization, statistic-bearing situation or personal real-life experience used to support its point. Return 0 if the list is valid and nonempty but no comment does so (purely abstract reasoning, hypotheticals, or generic claims). Hypothetical/invented scenarios do not count. Do not require external verification. Examples are nonexhaustive. Ignore the conversation column and any OP replies. Return 0 for a valid empty list; null if OC_comments is missing or malformed.

decomposed.h0: any_comment_concrete_real_world_example has zero association with the likelihood of view change (delta).
decomposed.h1: any_comment_concrete_real_world_example is positively associated with the likelihood of view change (delta).
decomposed.note: The "relying primarily on abstract reasoning" comparison group is operationalized as the absence of any concrete example comment; no frequency or dominance cutoff is specified, so "primarily" is not separately measured. Linear probability model via OLS. Comment order and chronology are unknown.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where counter-arguments explicitly engage with the specific examples or premises cited in the original argument text are associated with a higher likelihood of view change.

features.name: any_comment_engages_op_examples_or_premises
features.definition: Counter-argument comments (other users): any comment explicitly engages with a specific example or premise cited in the OP's argument text
features.spec: Read title, argument (OP body, current text including marked edits) and OC_comments (JSON list of comments by other users; order carries no meaning) jointly. Return 1 if at least one comment explicitly engages (e.g., addresses, questions, rebuts, accepts, or builds on) a specific example or premise that the OP cited in the argument text, identifiable by reference to that example/premise (quoting, paraphrasing, or directly naming it). Generic topical replies, or new arguments not tied to a cited OP example/premise, do not count. Engagement need not be critical. Return 0 if the list is valid and empty or no comment does so. Return null if argument or OC_comments is missing/malformed, or if OP context is insufficient to determine the target. Do not use conversation or any outcome.

decomposed.h0: any_comment_engages_op_examples_or_premises has no association with view change (coefficient = 0).
decomposed.h1: any_comment_engages_op_examples_or_premises is associated with higher likelihood of view change (coefficient > 0).
decomposed.note: Hypothesis says "counter-arguments" without specifying any/all/share; operationalized as any comment. OLS on binary outcome (linear probability). The conversation column is avoided because of outcome leakage.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions featuring counter-arguments that introduce concrete, personal labor-process details are associated with higher view-change rates than those relying solely on abstract normative principles.

features.name: any_comment_concrete_personal_labor_details
features.definition: Counter-argument comments (OC_comments): any comment introduces concrete, personal labor-process details (first-hand specifics of how work is actually done or experienced).
features.spec: Read the OC_comments JSON list (comments by users other than the OP; ignore order). Return 1 if at least one comment itself introduces concrete, personal details of a labor process, i.e. specific first-hand or personally situated descriptions of how work is actually done or experienced (tasks, procedures, workplace conditions, hours, tools, job steps) from the commenter's own or a specific person's work experience. Return 0 if no comment does (including only abstract, general or normative statements about labor). Exclude quoted text from others and bot/moderator notices unless the commenter adopts it as their own. Do not require verification. Valid empty list -> 0; missing or malformed OC_comments -> null.

features.name: all_comments_solely_abstract_normative
features.definition: Counter-argument comments (OC_comments): every comment relies solely on abstract normative principles, with no concrete personal labor-process details.
features.spec: Read the OC_comments JSON list (comments by users other than the OP; ignore order). Return 1 if the list is nonempty and the counter-arguments rely solely on abstract normative principles (general claims about what is right, fair, or ought to be, e.g. rights, justice, duty) and none introduces concrete personal or specific labor-process details or other concrete examples. Return 0 if any comment contains concrete details or non-normative argumentation. Exclude quoted text from others and bot/moderator notices unless adopted. Valid empty list -> null; missing or malformed OC_comments -> null.

Frequency/amount of detail is unspecified. conversation not used to avoid leakage. Prompt features are meant to be mutually exclusive by definition.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where counter-arguments explicitly quantify systemic material harms to third parties rather than asserting propositional falsity are associated with a higher likelihood of view change.

features.name: any_comment_quantifies_systemic_third_party_harm
features.definition: Counter-argument comments (OC_comments, not OP): 1 if any comment explicitly quantifies systemic material harms to third parties, else 0

Return 1 if at least one comment itself asserts that the OP's claim, or a specific proposition in the OP's post, is false, incorrect or logically invalid (propositional falsity). decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where counter-arguments identify logical contradictions within the original post's own stated premises are associated with higher view-change rates than those citing external evidence.

features.name: any_comment_identifies_op_premise_contradiction

features.spec: Read OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than the OP), jointly with the OP title and argument as the target. features.spec: Read OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than the OP). decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where the original argument uses hedging or qualifying language are associated with a higher likelihood of view change than those using absolute declarative statements.

features.name: op_argument_uses_hedging
features.definition: OP argument text (post body, current text incl. marked edits; excluding quoted external text): 1 if the OP uses hedging or qualifying language in their own assertions
features.spec: Read the 'argument' column only. Return 1 if the OP, in their own voice, uses hedging or qualifying language that softens or limits the strength of a claim (e.g. 'I think', 'maybe', 'perhaps', 'in most cases', 'might', 'to my knowledge', 'generally'); these are nonexhaustive examples. Ignore hedges inside quotations of others or in non-claim text. Use the current text including marked edits. Return 0 if the argument is assessable and has no such language. Return null if argument is missing or empty/malformed.

features.name: op_argument_uses_absolute_statements
features.definition: OP argument text (post body, current text incl. marked edits; excluding quoted external text): 1 if the OP makes absolute declarative statements stated as unqualified certainties
features.spec: Read the 'argument' column only. Return 1 if the OP, in their own voice, makes at least one absolute declarative statement: a claim asserted flatly as certain or universal without qualification (e.g. 'always', 'never', 'everyone', 'obviously', 'it is a fact that', or a bare categorical assertion); examples nonexhaustive. Ignore quoted external text. Use the current text including marked edits. Return 0 if assessable and none present. Return null if argument is missing or empty/malformed. decomposed.note: Hedging and absolute statements are not mutually exclusive, so the claimed contrast (hedged vs absolute-declarative arguments) is only approximated; the hedging coefficient is net of absolute statements, not an exact hedged-only vs absolute-only comparison. Binary presence, no frequency cutoff specified. Outcome is delta, added automatically (OLS linear probability).

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where counter-arguments explicitly quote the original poster's text rather than paraphrasing are associated with a higher probability of view change.

Endorsement or refutation is not required. Paraphrases without quoted wording, quotes of other commenters, external sources, or moderator/bot notices do not count. Return 0 if the list is valid and nonempty and no comment contains such a quote. Return 0 for a valid empty list. Return null if OC_comments is missing/malformed or if OP title and argument are both missing so that a negative cannot be established (a clear positive match to available OP text still gives 1). Do not use the conversation column or any outcome.

decomposed.h0: any_comment_quotes_op_text has no association with probability of view change.
decomposed.h1: any_comment_quotes_op_text is positively associated with probability of view change.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions containing counter-arguments that explicitly validate the original poster's emotional experience prior to logical rebuttal are associated with higher view-change rates.

features.definition: Any counter-argument comment: explicitly validates the OP's emotional experience (e.g., acknowledges feelings as understandable/legitimate) before presenting its logical rebuttal
features.spec: Read OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than the OP; order carries no chronology or rank) jointly with title and argument (OP context identifying the OP's emotional experience). Output 0 if no comment does so (generic politeness, praise, agreement with facts, or validation placed only after or without a rebuttal does not count; validation of the OP's reasoning rather than emotion does not count). Ignore quoted text from others unless adopted by the commenter. Use current supplied text. If OC_comments is a valid empty list output 0; if missing/malformed or OP context is missing so the judgment cannot be made, output null. Do not use conversation or any outcome.

decomposed.note: Hypothesis says "counter-arguments" (plural) without a frequency rule; operationalized as any comment. Order within a comment is judged from text; list order is not used. Linear probability model on binary delta.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions containing counter-arguments that use analogies to familiar scenarios are associated with a higher likelihood of the original poster changing their view.

features.name: title_absolute_quantifier
features.definition: OP title: explicitly contains an absolute universal quantifier or absolute-frequency term (e.g., all, never, always, every, none, no one) used to quantify the claim
features.spec: Read only the title. features.name: title_variable_probabilistic_term
features.definition: OP title: explicitly contains a variable or probabilistic quantifier term (e.g., some, often, sometimes, usually, most, generally, may, might, probably, likely)

Return 1 if the title text itself explicitly contains a variable or probabilistic term (such as some, many, most, often, sometimes, usually, generally, typically, may, might, probably, likely, rarely) that qualifies the claim's scope or certainty; the word must be used in that sense. Return 0 if none. Return null if title is missing or empty. Examples are nonexhaustive. Judged independently of whether an absolute term is also present.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions containing counter-arguments that explicitly reference specific, concrete examples or real-world instances in the provided comments are associated with a higher probability of view change.

decomposed.h1: Discussions with ack_component_before_counterexample = 1 have a higher view change rate than those with 0.
decomposed.note: Any-comment interpretation; hypothesis does not specify frequency. Binary outcome modeled with OLS (linear probability). Comment order is unknown, so acknowledgment-before-counterexample is judged only within a single comment.

decomposed.hypothesis: Counter-arguments frequently embedding direct quotations from the original post are associated with a higher likelihood of view change than those lacking explicit textual anchoring.

features.name: share_comments_quoting_op

decomposed.h0: Among posts receiving either, posters with any_substantive_counterargument =1 have the same view-change rate as those with only_supportive_comments =1.
decomposed.h1: Posts with any_substantive_counterargument =1 have a higher view-change rate than posts with only_supportive_comments =1.
decomposed.note: The claim compares two named groups (substantive counterargument vs only supportive). A single coefficient in the available rhs does not represent that contrast: with both indicators, the reference is neither group, and the claim corresponds to beta_A - beta_B, not one coefficient. Subsetting to the two groups cannot be expressed in the rhs. The dataset consists of counter-argument comments, so the only-supportive group is likely very small or empty. "Substantive" has no numeric threshold. Outcome delta is not used in measurement.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions containing specific counter-arguments citing empirical examples are more likely to be associated with original poster view change than those lacking such evidence.

features.name: any_comment_cites_empirical_example
features.definition: Counter-argument comments (OC_comments): any comment makes a specific counter-argument that cites an empirical example
features.spec: Read the JSON list in OC_comments (comments by users other than OP). Return 1 if at least one comment presents a specific counter-argument against the OP's view that cites a concrete empirical example (e.g., a specific real-world case, event, study, statistic, or documented observation) in support. Examples are nonexhaustive; no external verification needed. Purely abstract, hypothetical, or opinion-only reasoning does not count. Return 0 if the list is valid and no comment qualifies. Empty list gives 0. Null if OC_comments is missing or malformed. Do not use other columns.

decomposed.h0: any_comment_cites_empirical_example has no association with delta (coefficient = 0).
decomposed.h1: any_comment_cites_empirical_example is positively associated with delta (coefficient > 0).
decomposed.note: Association only, not causal. "Specific" and "empirical example" are judged semantically without a fixed frequency threshold. Comment order is unordered; conversation is not used to avoid leakage.

decomposed.hypothesis: Posts where the original poster explicitly requests emotional support or assistance in the argument text are less likely to result in a view change.

features.name: op_requests_emotional_support_or_assistance
features.definition: OP argument text: OP explicitly requests emotional support or assistance (1/0)
features.spec: Read the argument column (OP post body, current text including marked edits). Return 1 if the OP, in their own voice, explicitly asks for emotional support or for help/assistance (e.g., asking readers for comfort, support, help coping, or help with their situation). Return 0 if no such explicit request appears. Exclude quoted text from others and moderator/bot notices unless the OP adopts it. A request merely to change the OP's view does not by itself count; the request must be explicitly for emotional support or assistance. Return null if argument is missing or malformed.

decomposed.h0: Posts with op_requests_emotional_support_or_assistance = 1 have the same or higher probability of view change (delta) than those with 0.
decomposed.h1: Posts with op_requests_emotional_support_or_assistance = 1 have lower probability of view change than those with 0.
decomposed.note: "Assistance" is broad; the spec treats explicit requests for help/support only, and a generic request to change the view is not counted. OLS on binary outcome is a linear probability model.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where counter-arguments introduce concrete, external factual analogies are associated with higher view-change rates than those relying solely on abstract logical refutation.

features.name: any_comment_concrete_external_analogy
features.definition: Counter-argument comments (OC_comments): any comment introduces a concrete, external factual analogy
features.spec: Read the OC_comments JSON list (comments by users other than the OP). Return 1 if at least one comment introduces a concrete analogy drawn from outside the OP's own scenario, based on a specific real-world case, event, fact or situation (e.g. a named or specific historical, scientific, legal or everyday case) used as a comparison to the issue being argued. Purely abstract reasoning, hypotheticals with no real-world factual basis, and mere restatement of the OP's own examples do not count. Return 0 if the list is valid and no comment does so. Return null if OC_comments is missing or malformed. Empty list gives 0. Use only OC_comments; do not use conversation or later replies.

features.name: all_comments_solely_abstract_logical_refutation
features.definition: Counter-argument comments (OC_comments): every comment relies solely on abstract logical refutation with no concrete external factual analogy
features.spec: Read the OC_comments JSON list. Return 1 if the list is nonempty and every comment argues only through abstract logical reasoning/refutation (e.g. definitions, logical structure, general principles) and none introduces a concrete, external factual analogy based on a specific real-world case, event or fact. Return 0 if the list is valid and at least one comment introduces such a concrete analogy or other concrete external example. Return null if OC_comments is missing, malformed or empty. Use only OC_comments.

decomposed.h0: any_comment_concrete_external_analogy has zero association with view-change rate (delta).
decomposed.h1: Discussions with any_comment_concrete_external_analogy=1 have higher view-change rates than those without.
decomposed.note: The claimed comparison group is discussions relying solely on abstract logical refutation, not all discussions without analogies. Discussions with neither (e.g. other styles of comment) fall in the baseline of the tested term, so the coefficient is analogy vs not-analogy, an approximation. The second feature measures the named comparison group, but including both in one regression is nearly collinear (the second is a subset of the first's zeros), so it is not in rhs; a subset test restricted to the two named groups would be required for exact fidelity. The 'solely abstract' boundary is semantic and unanchored by the hypothesis. Discussion-level association only; comment order and chronology unknown.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where the original argument exceeds one hundred words are associated with a lower likelihood of view change than shorter arguments.

features.name: argument_word_count
features.definition: OP argument (post body, current text incl. marked edits): number of whitespace-delimited words
features.spec: len(str(argument).split()) for the row's argument text, using the supplied current text including any marked edits. If argument is missing/null, return null. Empty string yields 0.

features.name: argument_over_100_words
features.definition: OP argument (post body, current text): 1 if word count is strictly greater than 100, else 0
features.spec: Compute n = len(str(argument).split()) on the supplied current argument text; return 1 if n > 100 else 0; null if argument is missing/null. Equivalent to argument_word_count > 100.

decomposed.h0: argument_over_100_words has no association with the likelihood of view change (delta).
decomposed.h1: Discussions with argument_over_100_words = 1 have a lower likelihood of view change than those with argument_over_100_words = 0.
decomposed.note: Words counted by whitespace splitting on supplied current argument text (includes marked edits; no initial snapshot). Only ~3% of rows are at or under 100 words, so the comparison group is small. OLS on binary delta is a linear probability model.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where the original post's argument explicitly acknowledges potential counterpoints are associated with a higher likelihood of the view changing.

features.name: op_acknowledges_counterpoints
features.definition: OP post body: 1 if the OP explicitly acknowledges potential counterpoints, objections or opposing considerations to their own view, else 0
features.spec: Read only the argument column (OP's post body, current text including marked edits; ignore title and comments). Return 1 if the OP, in their own voice, explicitly acknowledges that counterpoints, objections, counterarguments or opposing considerations to their view exist or might be raised (e.g. 'some may argue', 'I know the counterargument is...', 'admittedly the other side says...'), whether or not they rebut them. Return 0 if no such explicit acknowledgment appears. Merely stating a view, hedging without referring to opposing points, or inviting people to change their view generically does not count. Exclude quotations of others' text not adopted by the OP, and moderator/bot notices. Null if argument is missing or malformed.

decomposed.h0: op_acknowledges_counterpoints has no association with the likelihood of view change (delta).
decomposed.h1: op_acknowledges_counterpoints is positively associated with the likelihood of view change (delta).
decomposed.note: Uses current argument text including marked edits; initial snapshot unavailable. Linear probability model on binary outcome; no controls specified by the claim.

decomposed.hypothesis: Observed discussions with a higher log-transformed length measure are associated with a higher probability that the original poster changes their view.

features.name: log_length_measure
features.definition: Row: supplied log-transformed length measure (log_length) as given
features.spec: Return pd.to_numeric(df['log_length'], errors='coerce') per row; null if missing or non-numeric. Observed range approx 0.69 to 7.44; construction undocumented, used as supplied with no re-transformation.

decomposed.h0: log_length_measure has no association with the probability that the OP changes their view (delta).
decomposed.h1: Higher log_length_measure is associated with a higher probability that the OP changes their view.
decomposed.note: log_length construction is undocumented (unclear what text it measures); used as supplied. OLS on binary outcome is a linear probability model. Association only, not causal.

decomposed.hypothesis: Disclosures of personal emotional vulnerability in the original argument are associated with a higher likelihood of the original poster changing their view.

features.name: op_discloses_personal_emotional_vulnerability
features.definition: OP's own argument text: 1 if the OP discloses their own personal emotional vulnerability, else 0
features.spec: Read only the argument column (OP post body, current text including marked edits). Return 1 if the OP, in their own voice, discloses a personal emotional vulnerability about themselves (e.g., admitting fear, shame, anxiety, depression, loneliness, hurt, insecurity, helplessness or emotional struggle). Exclude quoted text from others, reported opponents' positions, moderator/bot notices, and hypothetical or generic statements about people in general, unless explicitly adopted as the OP's own experience. Mere opinions or anger without self-disclosed vulnerability do not count. Return 0 if the text is present and contains no such disclosure. Return null if argument is missing or malformed. Use no other columns.

decomposed.h0: op_discloses_personal_emotional_vulnerability has no association with the likelihood of the OP changing their view.
decomposed.h1: op_discloses_personal_emotional_vulnerability is positively associated with the likelihood of the OP changing their view.
decomposed.note: Linear probability model via OLS on binary delta. Observed association only. Argument is current text and may include edits; no initial snapshot is available. The hypothesis does not specify an intensity or frequency threshold, so any such disclosure counts.

decomposed.hypothesis: A counterargument containing specific empirical evidence is associated with a higher likelihood of the original poster awarding a delta.

features.name: any_comment_specific_empirical_evidence
features.definition: Counterargument comments (OC_comments): any comment contains specific empirical evidence
features.spec: Read the JSON list in OC_comments (comments by users other than the OP; order carries no meaning). Return 1 if at least one comment itself presents specific empirical evidence in support of its argument, e.g. concrete data, statistics, study or research findings, documented real-world cases or observations with specific details. Vague appeals, generic assertions, hypotheticals, personal opinion without concrete facts, or logical reasoning alone do not count. Do not require external verification of accuracy. Return 0 if the list is valid and no comment qualifies. Return null if OC_comments is missing or malformed. An empty valid list yields 0.

decomposed.h0: any_comment_specific_empirical_evidence has no association with the likelihood of delta.
decomposed.h1: any_comment_specific_empirical_evidence is associated with a higher likelihood of delta.
decomposed.note: Hypothesis says "a counterargument", interpreted as any comment in the row. The row-level delta may not be tied to the specific comment containing evidence. OLS is a linear probability model.

decomposed.hypothesis: Engaging with a well-reasoned counterargument correlates with a higher frequency of logical concession statements from the original poster in discussions.

features.name: any_comment_well_reasoned_counterargument
features.definition: Other users' comments: any comment presents a well-reasoned counterargument to the OP's view (title/argument)
features.spec: Read title, argument (OP view) and OC_comments (JSON list of comments by other users; order is not rank or chronology) jointly. Return 1 if at least one comment directly challenges the OP's stated view with a well-reasoned counterargument: clear, relevant, logically coherent reasoning or evidence that bears on the OP's actual claim, not mere assertion, insult, joke, off-topic remark or pure agreement. Return 0 if the list is valid but empty or no comment qualifies. Return null if OC_comments is missing/malformed or the OP view cannot be determined (title and argument both missing). Do not use any outcome or other columns.

features.name: op_logical_concession_count
features.definition: OP's own replies in the discussion: count of distinct logical concession statements (OP grants a counterpoint's logical validity or acknowledges a flaw/limit in own reasoning)
features.spec: Read conversation together with title and argument. Identify the OP's own replies in the conversation (OP is the author of the post; OP turns may lack a speaker tag or be replies to commenters; use title/argument for context; do not attribute commenters' text to the OP). Count distinct statements by the OP that logically concede: acknowledging that a counterpoint is valid/correct, that their reasoning has a flaw, exception or limitation, or that a point undermines part of their view. Exclude mere politeness/thanks, quoted or reported opponent positions not adopted by OP, moderator/bot notices, and unchanged restatements. Output a non-negative integer count (0 = OP replies present but no such concession). If conversation contains no OP replies that can be identified, output 0 when the conversation is validly present with no OP replies; output null if conversation is missing or malformed. Count of statements over the discussion, not normalised by length.

decomposed.h0: any_comment_well_reasoned_counterargument has no association with op_logical_concession_count.
decomposed.h1: Discussions with any_comment_well_reasoned_counterargument = 1 have higher op_logical_concession_count.
decomposed.note: Frequency is operationalized as a raw count per discussion (no cutoff; hypothesis gives none). OP replies in conversation are often untagged, so OP identification is imperfect. Conversation may include later replies/view-change leakage, but is required since OP concessions only appear there. "Engaging with" is read as presence of a well-reasoned counterargument among comments; OP engagement itself is not separately measured. Correlational only.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where counter-arguments contain specific numerical data or statistics are associated with a higher likelihood of original-poster view change than those relying on general assertions.

features.name: any_comment_cites_numerical_data
features.definition: Counter-argument comments (OC_comments): any comment contains specific numerical data or statistics supporting its argument
features.spec: Read the OC_comments JSON list (comments by users other than the OP). Return 1 if at least one comment contains specific numerical data or statistics (e.g., concrete figures, percentages, rates, counts, measured quantities, or cited statistical findings) used in its argument. Return 0 if the list is valid and nonempty but no comment has such specifics (general assertions, reasoning, or non-quantitative examples only; incidental numbers like list numbering or generic words such as 'one' do not count). Quoted OP text does not count unless the commenter supplies data. Return null if OC_comments is missing or malformed; a valid empty list returns 0. Do not use the conversation, later replies or any outcome.

decomposed.h0: any_comment_cites_numerical_data has no association with OP view change.
decomposed.h1: any_comment_cites_numerical_data is positively associated with OP view change.
